headline: Researchers at the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi have sent quantum signals and ordinary data together over a single 50-kilometre optical fibre.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a named university team and a stated distance, but one demonstration reported from a statement, with no outside review.
importance_line: Banks, government agencies and hospitals could one day get quantum-secure links over ordinary fibre, but this is a single demonstration under controlled conditions, reported from a university statement with no outside comment.
source: Rediff, citing an IIT Delhi statement
summary: Rediff reports, citing an IIT Delhi statement, that a team led by physics professor Bhaskar Kanseri sent entangled photons (particles of light whose states are linked, a resource for secure quantum communication) and ordinary data together over a 50 km optical fibre, and that the work was published in the journal Optics Communication. The challenge is that ordinary signals are far stronger and can disturb the delicate quantum ones; Kanseri says the two can coexist “under carefully controlled conditions”, which could make quantum networks cheaper and easier to build by sharing existing fibre.
